title: Hamilton police officer, man in hospital after 'exchange of gunfire'
subtitle: A man with a firearm confronted the officer as they responded to a 911 call, Hamilton police said in a post on X.
article: A Hamilton police officer and a man in his 30s are in hospital with injuries after an exchange of gunfire on Saturday.

Shortly before 5 p.m., a resident of an apartment building at 1964 Main Street West called police to report a man "acting in a threatening manner," Ontario's Special Investigations Unit said in a news release .
Hamilton police officers made their way to the 5th floor of the building where they interacted with a man.
"There was an exchange of gunfire, resulting in the both the man and an officer suffering gunshot wounds," the SIU said in the release.
The man, who is in his 30s, was hospitalized with life-threatening injuries and the officer was transported to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.
The SIU confirmed it has invoked its mandate to investigate the shooting, and the police watchdog has assigned six investigators and two forensic investigators to the case.
The SIU is asking anyone who may have information about its investigation, including video or photos, to contact the lead investigator at 1-800-787-8529 or online at siu.on.ca/en/appeals.php .
